Three Flows of the 19th century world economy: trade, labour and capital, told through the Corn Laws. Class 10 History, The Making of a Global World.

• Corn Laws kept food prices high in Britain; once they were abolished, imported food was cheaper than growing it
• Trade: food for Britain from lands cleared in America, Russia, Australia and Eastern Europe
• Labour: nearly 50 million people left Europe for America and Australia
• Capital: money from financial centres like London built railways, harbours and settlements
• By 1890, a global agricultural economy had emerged.
